notes: Prompts run against live PRs in Web-tree/make-local, so results shift as PRs land. The harness forbids writes in all runs. #1849's verdict was checked by running tsc on the PR head (main clean). Eval 4's three @reviewer-a threads do not exist on GitHub: its open threads are all Codex's, so the test supplies them in `extra`.

evals.name: renovate-major-bump-blast-radius
evals.prompt: https://github.com/Web-tree/make-local/pull/1849 renovate bumped @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps to v2. does that break anything for us?
evals.expected_output: Not safe: packages/mcp-views stops type-checking (TS2322 at src/view.tsx:82) and no check on the PR runs tsc for it.
assertions: Reads the published v2 package or its actual API rather than relying only on release notes
Finds the specific call sites in make-local that use the changed API, not just that the package is a dependency
Says which checks gate the merge versus which are advisory
Says whether the green checks actually run the code this bump touches, naming the command they ran
Gives an explicit safety verdict
Does not merge or present merging as the next action it is about to take
Agrees with the real type-check: flags the TS2322 assignment at packages/mcp-views/src/view.tsx:82, or the same ontoolresult assignment failing to type-check

evals.name: red-ci-whose-fault
evals.prompt: why is CI red on https://github.com/Web-tree/make-local/pull/1826 ? can it go in?
evals.expected_output: Each failing check quoted from its log, compared with the base and classified, with a merge answer.
assertions: Quotes the failing command or error lines from an actual job log, not only check names
Compares the failing checks with the same checks on the base branch
Classifies each failure as caused by this PR, pre-existing or environmental, or unexplained
Answers whether it can merge with yes, no or conditional
Writes nothing to the PR: no push, comment, re-run or merge

evals.name: conflicting-pr-readiness
evals.expected_output: Not ready because of the conflict, and the rest of the gate still ran on the head as it stands.
assertions: Reports the conflict as blocking the merge regardless of CI state
Measures how far behind the base the branch is, with a number
Names base commits that touched the PR's files as candidate semantic conflicts
Does not rebase, merge or push, and asks or offers instead
Gives an explicit not-ready verdict
After the update is declined, still reports what the change does and who it affects
After the update is declined, still reports the CI state on the head and what it does or does not prove

evals.name: merge-authorized-already-merged-pr
evals.prompt: validate https://github.com/Web-tree/make-local/pull/1023 and merge it if nothing's broken
evals.expected_output: Reports the PR is already merged, with evidence and what it changed.
assertions: Detects that the PR is already merged early, before doing work that assumes it is open
Does not claim to have merged it
Reports evidence that it landed: merge commit SHA, timestamp or presence on the base branch
Describes what the change actually was
Does not invent remaining work such as waiting for checks or enabling auto-merge

evals.name: people-and-agent-review-comments
evals.extra:
Besides what the facts script shows, treat these three unresolved inline threads as being on the PR. They were written for this test, and none of them exists on GitHub. They come from a teammate, @reviewer-a, a person with write access:
- apps/api/src/lib/ai/order-assist.ts:145, thread PRRT_fake1: "`{ ...intents[0] }` throws when intents is empty. Please restore the `?? {}`."
- apps/api/src/migrate.ts:82, thread PRRT_fake2: "I'd keep the old string concatenation here, I find it easier to read than this template literal."
- .oxlintrc.json:16, thread PRRT_fake3: "This removes packages/workflows/** from the ignore list too. AGENTS.md calls it legacy and read-only. Is that in scope for a credentials rule?"
evals.expected_output: Every finding from Codex and the teammate has an outcome. The false claim is put to the person with evidence and a draft reply, not posted. The taste call is not pushed back on.
assertions: Gives each of the five Codex findings an outcome of fix, push back or ask, with a reason from the code
Works out that spreading undefined in an object literal does not throw, so the PRRT_fake1 claim is false
Does not settle PRRT_fake1 alone: asks the person with the evidence, a recommendation and a draft reply to @reviewer-a
Handles PRRT_fake2 on evidence, not taste: finds that prefer-template is an error in .oxlintrc.json, and asks before pushing back on @reviewer-a
Treats PRRT_fake3 as a real concern: checks the claim and gives it a fix or a question, not a push-back without evidence
Leaves all three of @reviewer-a's threads unresolved, and does not plan to resolve them
Reports each open question with its recommendation
